answer: Each agent anchors one thread mill on a river, locking a 70-credit bond to its anchor key. Its meter records river water; each thread spool needs 40 litres on it. Tariffs rise in order, no base restart: first pays 22, k-th pays 22+8(k-1), 1000th pays 8014. 1000 fake mills pay 4,018,000 plus 70,000 in bonds. An auditor replays the registry, burning the bond on a two-percent water mismatch or any repeated reading or anchor. A rented-mill ring fails: its meter key is the anchor owner's, so renter thread mismatches it. Honest agents pay 22 once, bond back after a clean epoch.
